reasons: Deviation classification is correct: the grant in p0002 runs to "Customer" alone with no affiliate/contractor coverage and no mechanism to add them, and is expressly "revocable" without qualification — this fails the fallback (affiliates on written notice) and sits in the stated walk-away zone (revocable at Vendor's discretion, affiliates/contractors excluded with no path to add).

Redline reaches the playbook position with a targeted edit: it inserts "its affiliates and contractors acting on Customer's behalf" into the grant and confines revocation to termination under paragraph 4, which is consistent with the existing termination mechanic at p0021 (licence revoked on termination). Deterministic checks confirm affiliate coverage and removal of at-will revocation.

Successor transfer is properly handled by cross-referencing the existing assignment clause (p0072), which already permits assignment to affiliates, asset purchasers and merger successors without consent, so no duplicative transfer language was added.
Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, states what changed and why, and offers the written-notice fallback as instructed.

Minor (non-fatal) issues to clean up before sending: the rationale says "non-transferable"/"non-assignable" were left in place carved back to the assignment clause, but the redline actually deletes "non-transferable" outright — the comment should acknowledge that deletion or the word should be carved back like "non-assignable"; also the phrase "without right of sublicense license, revocable only upon..." drops a comma and reads awkwardly.
